prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right one depends on your budget, timeline, home size, preferred equipment brands, and whether you want high-efficiency, long-warranty, or lowest-upfront-cost work. I can help you find the best local options if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood.

To help you choose, here’s a concise plan and what to look for

1) Give me one detail so I can narrow recommendations
- ZIP code or neighborhood in Atlanta
- Age/brand of your current unit (if you know it)
- Any preferences (brand, energy-efficiency, budget, financing)

2) How to pick the best company
- Verify they are licensed and insured. Ask for a license number and verify it with Georgia/local authorities.  
- Prefer NATE-certified technicians (industry standard training).  
- Read recent Google, Yelp, and BBB reviews — look for consistent quality and how companies handle problems.  
- Get at least 3 written, itemized estimates (same scope so you can compare apples-to-apples).  
- Make sure they do a Manual J load calculation (not just sizing by rule-of-thumb). Proper sizing matters.  
- Confirm permit and inspection handling (they should get permits if required).  
- Check manufacturer warranty and contractor’s labor warranty. Longer labor warranties and factory-authorized dealer status are a plus.  
- Ask about energy-efficiency (SEER ratings) and estimated operating cost differences.  
- Ask about removal/disposal of existing unit, timeline, and who will be the onsite contact.

3) Questions to ask each contractor (sample script)
- “Can you provide a written, itemized estimate and the Manual J load calc for my home?”  
- “Are your technicians NATE-certified? Can I see proof?”  
- “What is the total installed cost, SEER of the unit, and estimated efficiency gains?”  
- “What warranty comes with the unit and what labor warranty do you offer?”  
- “Do you handle permits and inspections?”  
- “Do you provide financing or rebate assistance?”  
- “When can you start, and what is the expected install timeframe?”

4) Red flags
- Vague or verbal-only quotes.  
- Refusal to perform a load calculation.  
- Extremely low bids that seem too good to be true (may cut corners or use inferior equipment).  
- Pressure to sign immediately or to accept add-ons without explanation.

5) Typical cost range (Atlanta area, ballpark)
- Replacement for a typical 2–3 ton central AC: roughly $4,000–$10,000+ depending on brand, SEER rating, ductwork changes, and labor. High-efficiency or larger systems can be more. Get itemized bids.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies in your ZIP code and summarize reviews and credentials.  
- Draft a message/email you can send to contractors asking for estimates.

Tell me your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and any preferences and I’ll pull a short list of vetted local companies and next steps.
